meta.subtitle: Should src/ be renamed to cli/ and the CLI-specific files moved into one directory?
meta.summary: Pros, cons, and the recommended outcome: keep src/ — rename buys little and breaks Python ecosystem expectations.

blocks.summary: The rename feels appealing because every file under src/ is in fact CLI code. But the Python ecosystem treats src/<package>/ as the canonical layout — every tool (uv, pip, hatchling, ruff, mypy, pytest) recognises it without configuration. Renaming to cli/ saves zero confusion (the directory contents already say 'CLI') while requiring overrides in every tool, and the bin/ shim is a separate concern best left where it is.
bullets: Recommendation: keep src/, keep bin/html-doc, keep pyproject.toml at the repo root.
If the legibility concern is real, add a one-line README inside src/ saying 'this is the CLI source; the runtime is in kit/' — that solves the actual confusion at zero structural cost.
Reopen if a non-CLI Python module ever joins the codebase (then src/cli/ + src/<other>/ become natural).

blocks.title: Today's layout
blocks.lead: Every Python file lives under src/. Everything else at the root falls into one of: kit runtime, docs, examples, packaging, CI.

blocks.source:
html-doc/
├── bin/
│   └── html-doc                 ← PEP 723 shim (uv run bin/html-doc …)
├── src/
│   ├── html_doc/
│   │   ├── cli.py               ← the entire CLI: argparse, build, serve, check, init, clean
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   ├── assets/              ← copied from kit/ during build (force-include)
│   │   └── templates/           ← starter.{json,html}
│   └── html_doc_tests/          ← pytest suite (≈200 tests)
├── kit/                         ← runtime: chrome.js, chrome.css, renderer.js, schemas, glossary, extrefs
├── docs/                        ← the kit's own documentation pages
├── examples/                    ← demo projects rendered by the kit
├── pyproject.toml               ← packaging + dep + tool config
├── uv.lock
├── README.md
└── CLAUDE.md

blocks.title: Two languages, two homes
blocks.content: kit/ is the runtime (JS + CSS, what the browser executes). src/ is the build/serve toolchain (Python, what the CLI executes). The split is clean: kit/ ships to readers, src/ ships to authors. The proposed rename would blur this — readers don't need 'cli', the kit handles them.

blocks.title: Three candidate restructures
blocks.lead: Each weighed on legibility, Python-ecosystem cost, and downstream churn.

blocks.content: Keep src/html_doc/ as the package home. Keep bin/html-doc as the launcher. Keep pyproject.toml at the repo root. Optionally add a one-line README inside src/ explaining the boundary.

items: + Zero churn. No imports change, no CI changes, no install command changes.
+ Matches the documented Python `src layout` (pyproject.toml lives next to src/<package>/). uv, pip, hatchling, ruff, mypy, pytest all recognise this without configuration.
+ Consistent with the existing wheel: `pip install html-doc` already installs the `html_doc` package — the on-disk directory matches the importable name.
− Costs the maintainer the urge to make 'src' say what's in it.
− If a future non-CLI Python module ever joins, the urge will return.

blocks.content: Pure directory rename. Package name stays html_doc; the only change is the parent directory.

items: + Directory name now hints at the contents.

− Every Python tool that auto-detects src/ now needs a config override. pyproject.toml gains `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ["cli/html_doc"]`. Same for ruff (`src = ["cli"]`), pytest (`pythonpath = ["cli"]`), mypy if used.
− Breaks editor / IDE discovery heuristics that look at `src/` first.
− Doesn't solve the actual problem (a reader doesn't open src/ wondering 'is this kit code or CLI code?' — that gets answered by the file's first line).
− Cost is paid by every contributor who knows the standard layout and now has to learn this one.

blocks.title: C — Move bin/, pyproject.toml, and src/ all into a cli/ subdir

blocks.content: Maximalist version: cli/ contains pyproject.toml, src/html_doc/, bin/html-doc, uv.lock. The repo root holds only kit/, docs/, examples/, README.md, CLAUDE.md.

items: + Clean conceptual split at the top level: kit (runtime) vs cli (toolchain) vs docs (content).
− Install command becomes `uv tool install ./cli` instead of `uv tool install .`. Every README, CI workflow, and IDE preset must learn this exception.
− pyproject.toml inside a subdir breaks one-line shortcut tools that assume the root (`pip install .`, `uv run --project .`).
− Worktree / IDE roots that pin to the repo top see a `cli/` they have to descend into; the repo no longer 'looks like' a Python project at the top.
− The bin/ shim has its own UNIX convention (executable entrypoints at the top); burying it inside cli/ doesn't help discoverability.

blocks.title: The Python-ecosystem cost of moving src/
blocks.lead: Every tool that auto-discovers source needs a config override the moment you stop using src/.

rows: Walks pyproject.toml; picks up src layout if hatchling configured
rootdir + sys.path auto-includes src/ via importlib mode
Treats src/ as first-party module root
Per-IDE config; not portable across contributors

blocks.title: Cost asymmetry
blocks.content: Keeping src/ costs zero configuration. Moving it costs configuration in every tool that ever touches Python code. Each override is small individually; the aggregate is a layer of "why does this repo not just work?" friction that every new contributor (and every new tool) hits forever.

blocks.title: What the rename doesn't actually fix
blocks.lead: The premise of the rename is that 'src' is generic and doesn't say what's inside. But that confusion isn't real in this repo — the rename would replace a non-confusion with friction.

items: A reader entering the repo sees kit/, src/, docs/, examples/ at the top. The naming pattern is already 'runtime / source / content / demos' — every Python-aware reader maps src/ to 'source' instantly.

Inside src/, the package is named html_doc — same as the wheel they'd install. The package's contents are cli.py + templates/ + assets/ + tests. A reader opens cli.py and sees the argparse setup in the first 200 lines. No naming change to the parent directory would explain that faster.
If the worry is 'what if I add a non-CLI Python module later?' — the answer is `src/html_doc/<new_module>.py` (a sibling to cli.py). No directory restructure required.

blocks.title: What about bin/html-doc?
blocks.lead: Separate question, separate answer. The shim is a UNIX convention — leave it at the top.

cards.title: Keep bin/html-doc at the repo root
items: UNIX-shaped expectation: project executables live in bin/.

PEP 723 inline-script metadata in bin/html-doc is the file's primary purpose — it has to be a single executable file users can run with `uv run bin/html-doc`. Burying it in src/ contradicts the shape.
The shim is tiny (one file, no dependencies on its location).

cards.title: Move bin/ inside src/ or cli/
items: Breaks the UNIX convention contributors expect.
Doesn't reduce the number of top-level entries — replaces bin/ with one fewer top-level dir, but only at the cost of harder-to-find executables.
Users running `uv run path/to/html-doc` need a stable, top-level path.

blocks.title: What about pyproject.toml?
blocks.lead: Has to stay at the root. Moving it makes the repo no longer a discoverable Python project.

items: uv, pip, build, ruff, pytest, every Python-aware tool searches the cwd for pyproject.toml. Moving it under cli/ means every one of those commands needs the path explicitly or a wrapper script.
GitHub's repo-language detection uses pyproject.toml at the root to classify the project. Burying it makes the repo show up as JavaScript-first (kit/ dominates the line count).
Editors that use 'open project' on the repo root would no longer find the package metadata.

blocks.title: Recommendation
blocks.lead: Keep the current layout. Add a single small marker to make the boundary explicit.

steps.title: No rename
steps.content: src/ stays. bin/ stays. pyproject.toml stays at the root. The rename neither earns its churn cost nor solves a real confusion.

steps.title: Add src/README.md
steps.content: A four-line marker explaining the boundary: 'This directory contains the html-doc CLI source — the toolchain that builds and serves docs. The runtime (chrome.js, chrome.css, renderer.js) lives in ../kit/.' Settles the question for any reader who arrives via the directory tree rather than the README.

steps.title: Revisit only on real second-module pressure
steps.content: If a second non-CLI Python module ever joins the codebase (e.g., a shared library used by both the CLI and an external integration), the natural next step is `src/html_doc/cli/` + `src/html_doc/<other>/` — still within the standard layout.

items: Should src/html_doc/cli.py itself be split? It's ~2400 lines covering init / build / serve / check / clean plus the markdown converter and the dev server. The single-file shape is convenient for `bin/html-doc` (PEP 723 inline script) but pressure to split will grow if the file passes 3000 lines. Separate plan if it becomes painful.

Should html_doc_tests/ move into a top-level tests/ directory? The Python standard practice splits tests out of src/. Today they live alongside the package which means the wheel ships test files — minor footgun. Worth a separate small refactor.
Should bin/ contain more than one entry? Possible future shims (a docs-LLM wrapper, a syntax converter) would all live there. Not blocking until those exist.
